Additional details about Abdullah's troubled past were also revealed, including the fact that she had reportedly been a victim of human trafficking and spent the past two years in a group home. In 2022, Abdullah's social media accounts became active again, indicating that she was once again released from custody. On Instagram, she revealed to her followers that she had Jacqueline's name tattooed across her chest. Interestingly, it appears that everything on her account prior to the accident has been deleted. She also added the comment, Love to this picture of a T-shirt reading, free Abdullah Sanchez. Abdullah also posted this image of Jacqueline, trying on what might be the Kinsenera dress she never got to wear, and mentioned memorializing her sister for Dia de los Mertos. She followed up with this picture of her sister's grave, decorated for the occasion with the caption, Rest easy until we meet again. She also talked about making special plans for her sister's birthday that year and shared this photo of Jacqueline beside a lake with the hashtag, long-lived Jackie. But there's a dark irony in the difference between Abdullah's posts about her sister and her day-to-day content. Abdulia also posted this video of herself with what appears to be alcohol in a vehicle. Her caption, It's All Gone, raises concerns. Considering all of this, it might not be that surprising to hear that Abdullah was arrested yet again in 2003, after she was once again identified as a felon in possession of a firearm. She posted this image of her official jail ID with the caption, Free Me, shortly after her arrest. Tragically, Abdullah's arrests and run-ins with the law have not only affected her, but also the people closest to her, like her sister, Jacqueline.
